title: Lesson 1 - Data 360 Terminology: Data Streams, Data Lake Objects, Data Model Objects, and the Three Stages
description: Describe Data 360's key terminology and business value, covering the core constructs (data streams, data lake objects, data model objects, data spaces, data graphs, unified profiles) and the three processing stages they live in.

questions.question: A new consultant is asked to describe, in order, the stages data moves through in Data 360. Which sequence is correct?
options: Connect Data, Harmonize and Unify, Analyze and Act
Harmonize and Unify, Connect Data, Analyze and Act
Analyze and Act, Connect Data, Harmonize and Unify
Connect Data, Analyze and Act, Harmonize and Unify
questions.explanation: Data always starts with Connect Data, then Harmonize and Unify, then Analyze and Act. The strongest distractor swaps the first two steps, but you cannot harmonize data that has not been connected.

questions.question: After a stream runs, where do the ingested rows land first, and what is the standardized layer called?
options: A data model object, then a data lake object
A data lake object, then a data model object after mapping
A data graph, then a segment
A unified profile, then a calculated insight
questions.explanation: Ingested rows land in a data lake object, and you map DLO fields to a DMO to harmonize them, so the correct order is DLO then DMO. The first option reverses the order, and a data graph is a precomputed view, not a landing zone.

questions.question: Which statement about a unified profile is correct?
options: It overwrites the source records with the winning values
It is a set of keys that links matching records without changing source data
It only holds fields from a single source
It is created by a data transform, not by identity resolution
questions.explanation: Identity resolution links records into a unified profile and never overwrites source data, while reconciliation only decides what displays. The first option confuses reconciliation with a golden-record overwrite, which is not how Data 360 works.
